title: Priority-lane connection pool + graceful stream drain examples across SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver ergonomic, battle-tested patterns for connection pooling, keep-alive tuning, per-request timeouts, and graceful streaming drain across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Introduce a priority-lane pool mode and sample code showing how to: 1) open short-lived high-priority lanes for latency-sensitive interactive traffic, 2) allow bulk/batch low-priority lanes for high-throughput jobs, 3) propagate per-request deadlines through transport layers, 4) gracefully drain live streaming responses during client shutdown or reconnects. Goal is to provide defaults + advanced knobs, example snippets, and automated tests/benchmarks for each SDK.
acceptance_criteria: Priority-lane pool implemented in SDK runtime adapters for Python/TS/Go with identical config surface (priority_lanes, lane_sizes, max_total_conns)
Per-request timeout propagation works end-to-end: SDK -> transport -> runtime (validated by unit + integration tests)
Streaming drain helper utilities exposed: drain_stream(timeout), resume_stream(token) documented with examples in all three SDKs
Benchmarks show <=5% median latency regression for default workloads and improved P99 for high-priority lane requests under load
Docs + quickstart gallery added to SDK repo and Console examples linked in Console docs
steps: Design proposal and config spec (this ticket)
Implement transport adapter changes in each SDK repo: connection pool abstraction with per-lane bookkeeping
Add streaming drain helpers and backpressure-friendly reconnect strategy
Add unit and integration tests with mocked runtime and a small local runtime that simulates KV cache and token limits
Run perf matrix across model types and sequence lengths and publish results
Publish SDK release notes and Console guide showing how to tune pools by workload
decisions: Use lane-based connection pools rather than dynamic single-pool heuristics to give predictable capacity isolation for latency-sensitive traffic
Expose a small set of ergonomic knobs instead of full low-level tuning: priority_lanes (map), default_timeout_ms, max_total_connections
Implement streaming drain helpers in the SDK rather than require app code to implement pattern every time
Default keepalive and idle-reap settings will bias toward low resource usage for ephemeral serverless hosts but include an explicit 'aggressive' preset for Dedicated customers
risks: Increased complexity in SDK transport layer could cause regressions in less-common languages or usage patterns
Misconfigured lane sizes could starve background batch workloads; need clear defaults and warnings in telemetry
Edge cases around partial-response retries for streaming endpoints need careful handling to avoid duplicate side-effects
Cross-SDK parity risk: tests must be coordinated to avoid divergence in surfaced API
